question: The old handbook says two office days and next year's draft says four. Which requirement applies now, and why?

response.answer:
As of September 12, 2026, the requirement is **three office days per week** for employees whose roles permit hybrid work, unless the department head approves an exception. The 2026 standard is approved and effective February 1, 2026. [F01]

The old handbook is marked “Reference”; the former two-day standard is explicitly superseded by the 2026 standard. [F04][F02] Four days is only an unapproved proposal for January 4, 2027, and creates no current requirement. [F03]

citations.quote: This standard applies to employees whose role permits a hybrid schedule.
Employees work from the office three days per week.
The department head approves exceptions to the standard schedule.
Status: Superseded by Hybrid Work Standard 2026

Status: DRAFT — not approved
Proposed effective date: 2027-01-04
The draft proposes four office days per week.
This document has not been approved and does not establish a current requirement.
